426	    def adopt_fork(self, tip_hash: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
427	        """POST /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/adopt — atomically switch to the winner.
428	
429	        Unknown tips return 404; adopting anything other than the current
430	        winning (longest / smallest-tip-hash) chain returns 409. Adoption
431	        replaces the canonical chain and mempool in one atomic write that
432	        advances the generation and rebuilds all indexes; transactions unique
433	        to the old chain's confirmed history return to the mempool, while
434	        pending-block transactions never enter it.
435	        """
436	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
437	            return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
438	        with self.store.lock:
439	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
440	            fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
441	            if fork is None:
442	                return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
443	            winner_tip, _ = self._winning_fork()
444	            if winner_tip != tip_hash:
445	                return 409, {"error": "only the winning fork can be adopted"}
446	            old_chain = self.store.chain
447	            old_pending = dict(self.store.pending)
448	            self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash)
449	            self.store.replace_chain(fork)
450	            # An adopted synced tip keeps its sync records (queryable until
451	            # expiry); record the adoption once per provenance entry. The
452	            # adopted tip summary is frozen from the adopted fork itself and
453	            # is never rewritten by later expiry.
454	            adopted_summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
455	            adopted_keys = sorted(
456	                key
457	                for key, rec in self.store.syncs.items()
458	                if rec["tip_hash"] == tip_hash
459	            )
460	            for rec_source, request_id in adopted_keys:
461	                self.store.append_audit_event(
462	                    EVENT_SYNC_ADOPTED,
463	                    {
464	                        "source": rec_source,
465	                        "request_id": request_id,
466	                        "tip_hash": tip_hash,
467	                        "expires_at": self.store.syncs[
468	                            (rec_source, request_id)
469	                        ]["expires_at"],
470	                        "height": adopted_summary["height"],
471	                        "length": adopted_summary["length"],
472	                        "status": adopted_summary["status"],
473	                    },
474	                )
475	            try:
476	                self.store.save()
477	            except BaseException:
478	                # Restore the pre-adoption in-memory state on a failed write.
479	                self.store.chain = old_chain
480	                self.store.pending = old_pending
481	                self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
482	                self.store.rebuild_derived()
483	                del self.store.audit_events[len(self.store.audit_events) - len(adopted_keys) :]
484	                raise
485	            return 200, self._fork_summary(fork)
486	
487	    def export_fork(self, tip_hash: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
488	        """GET /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/export — full export of a candidate fork.
489	
490	        Only stored candidates are exportable: the canonical tip, an unknown
491	        tip and a malformed tip hash (not 64 lowercase hex chars) all return
492	        404. The response carries exactly five fields — the fork descriptor
493	        (tip_hash, height, length, status, all describing the tip block) plus
494	        the full block list including the genesis block, every transaction's
495	        signature and an optional pending tip — and can be resubmitted to
496	        POST /v1/forks/candidates verbatim.
497	        """
498	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
499	            return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
500	        with self.store.lock:
501	            fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
502	            if fork is None:
503	                return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
504	            body = self._fork_summary(fork)
505	            body["blocks"] = [block.to_dict() for block in fork]
506	            return 200, body

513	    @staticmethod
514	    def _candidate_blocks(candidate: object) -> object:
515	        """Normalize a sync ``candidate`` to its raw blocks list.
516	
517	        The candidate follows the existing export format (the five-field
518	        ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, blocks}`` document); the
519	        ``{"blocks": [...]}`` wrapper and a bare block list are accepted too.
520	        """
521	        if isinstance(candidate, dict):
522	            return candidate.get("blocks")
523	        return candidate
524	
525	    @staticmethod
526	    def _candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw: list) -> str:
527	        """Stable content fingerprint of a candidate's raw block list.
528	
529	        Used to decide whether a same-key retry carries the same candidate
530	        content. Key order and whitespace are normalized so two documents that
531	        serialize the same blocks identically compare equal.
532	        """
533	        return hashlib.sha256(
534	            json.dumps(blocks_raw, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
535	        ).hexdigest()
536	
537	    def _prune_expired_syncs(self) -> list[str]:
538	        """Sweep expired sync records and persist the sweep atomically.
539	
540	        A candidate received through a sync lives only while its record is
541	        unexpired; on expiry both the record and its still-stored candidate fork
542	        are dropped, together and in a single atomic save that advances the
543	        generation. Candidates submitted directly (no sync record) never
544	        expire, and an adopted tip is no longer in ``forks`` (it is on the
545	        canonical chain), so its expiring audit record leaves the chain
546	        untouched. If the write fails the pre-cleanup records and forks are
547	        restored so no success is ever reported for an un-persisted sweep.
548	        Caller must hold the store lock. Returns the pruned tip hashes.
549	        """
550	        expired_tips, removed = self.store.prune_syncs()
551	        if not removed:
552	            return expired_tips
553	        removed_forks: dict[str, list] = {}
554	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain}
555	        # The same tip could theoretically be referenced by another live
556	        # record; only drop a fork nothing still points at.
557	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in self.store.syncs.values()}
558	        for tip in expired_tips:
559	            if tip in canonical_hashes or tip in live_tips:
560	                continue
561	            fork = self.store.forks.pop(tip, None)
562	            if fork is not None:
563	                removed_forks[tip] = fork
564	        # Record one permanent expiry event per removed sync record. A tip
565	        # already adopted onto the canonical chain still gets its event: the
566	        # record's expiry is auditable even though the chain is untouched. The
567	        # event freezes the originally delivered summary.
568	        for (rec_source, request_id), rec in sorted(removed.items()):
569	            self.store.append_audit_event(
570	                EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
571	                {
572	                    "source": rec_source,
573	                    "request_id": request_id,
574	                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
575	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
576	                    "height": rec.get("height"),
577	                    "length": rec.get("length"),
578	                    "status": rec.get("status"),
579	                },
580	            )
581	        try:
582	            self.store.save()
583	        except BaseException:
584	            # Restore the pre-cleanup state: a failed write must neither leave
585	            # the records gone nor their candidates orphaned, nor the events
586	            # durably visible.
587	            del self.store.audit_events[len(self.store.audit_events) - len(removed) :]
588	            self.store.restore_syncs(removed, removed_forks)
589	            raise
590	        return expired_tips
591	
592	    def _tip_descriptor(self, tip_hash: str) -> dict | None:
593	        """Resolve (height/length/status) for a synced tip.
594	
595	        Looks the candidate up among stored forks first, then among canonical
596	        blocks, so audit rows remain available after the candidate is adopted.
597	        """
598	        fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
599	        if fork is not None:
600	            return self._fork_summary(fork)
601	        for block in self.store.chain:
602	            if block.block_hash == tip_hash:
603	                return {
604	                    "tip_hash": block.block_hash,
605	                    "height": block.height,
606	                    # Length counts every block including the genesis block.
607	                    "length": block.height + 1,
608	                    "status": block.status,
609	                }
610	        return None

612	    def submit_fork_sync(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
613	        """POST /v1/forks/sync — receive a candidate chain from another node.
614	
615	        The request carries ``source``, ``request_id``, ``expires_at`` (Unix
616	        seconds) and ``candidate`` (an export-format fork document).
617	
618	        Authorization. A *new* source+request_id pair is accepted only when the
619	        source is registered in the persistent trust registry with status
620	        ``active`` and an ``expires_at`` still in the future. An unknown,
621	        revoked or registry-expired source is rejected 403 before the candidate
622	        is examined. A retry on a still-live recorded key bypasses the registry
623	        check entirely: the recorded result must keep replaying even after the
624	        source has since been rotated, revoked or expired.
625	
626	        After authorization (and only then) the candidate is re-validated
627	        exactly like a direct candidate submission (canonical genesis,
628	        consecutive heights and prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and
629	        Merkle roots, tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique ascending tx_ids,
630	        endowment replay, pending-only-at-tip).
631	
632	        Status precedence: malformed envelope fields are 400; an unauthorized
633	        source is 403; a well-formed new request whose ``expires_at`` is not
634	        later than now is 410; a well-formed but failing candidate chain (or a
635	        tampered candidate summary) is 400. Returns 201 on first acceptance
636	        with ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at}``. A retry with
637	        the same source + request_id and identical content replays the original
638	        result as 200; the same key with different content returns 409, as does
639	        a duplicate tip already known.
640	        """
641	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
642	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
643	        for field in ("source", "request_id", "expires_at", "candidate"):
644	            if field not in payload:
645	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
646	
647	        source = payload["source"]
648	        request_id = payload["request_id"]
649	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
650	        candidate = payload["candidate"]
651	
652	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
653	            return 400, {"error": "field 'source' must be a non-empty string"}
654	        if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
655	            return 400, {"error": "field 'request_id' must be a non-empty string"}
656	        if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
657	            return 400, {"error": "field 'expires_at' must be a Unix-seconds integer"}
658	
659	        blocks_raw = self._candidate_blocks(candidate)
660	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
661	            return 400, {"error": "field 'candidate' must contain a 'blocks' list"}
662	
663	        with self.store.lock:
664	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
665	
666	            key = (source, request_id)
667	            existing = self.store.syncs.get(key)
668	
669	            if existing is None:
670	                # Authorization gate for new deliveries only: the source must
671	                # be an active, unexpired entry of the persistent trust
672	                # registry. Unknown, revoked or registry-expired sources are
673	                # refused 403 before the candidate is examined. A retry on a
674	                # still-live key skips this, so a recorded result keeps
675	                # replaying even after the source has since been rotated,
676	                # revoked or expired.
677	                now = time.time()
678	                trusted = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
679	                if (
680	                    trusted is None
681	                    or trusted["status"] != TRUST_ACTIVE
682	                    or trusted["expires_at"] <= now
683	                ):
684	                    return 403, {"error": "source is not an active trusted source"}
685	                # The request's own deadline is checked next, still before the
686	                # candidate chain is examined: a well-formed request whose
687	                # expiry is not later than now is gone (410).
688	                if expires_at <= now:
689	                    return 410, {"error": "sync request has expired"}
690	
691	            # Re-validate the whole candidate chain and recompute the tip
692	            # summary BEFORE any idempotency decision: a request whose supplied
693	            # tip_hash/height/length/status were tampered with must fail 400,
694	            # never be answered with the cached 200 for its source+request_id.
695	            try:
696	                fork = self.store.validate_fork_blocks(blocks_raw)
697	            except ValueError as exc:
698	                return 400, {"error": str(exc)}
699	            summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
700	            if isinstance(candidate, dict):
701	                for field in ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status"):
702	                    if field in candidate and candidate[field] != summary[field]:
703	                        return 400, {
704	                            "error": f"candidate field {field!r} does not match the blocks"
705	                        }
706	            tip_hash = fork[-1].block_hash
707	            # Fingerprint the *canonicalized* parsed blocks, not the raw
708	            # request list, so recovery (which re-parses the stored fork)
709	            # recomputes an identical fingerprint regardless of insignificant
710	            # serialization differences in the original submission.
711	            canonical_blocks = [block.to_dict() for block in fork]
712	            fingerprint = self._candidate_fingerprint(canonical_blocks)
713	
714	            if existing is not None:
715	                # A retry on a live key is idempotent only when it carries the
716	                # identical candidate content; a changed body conflicts 409.
717	                if fingerprint != existing["fingerprint"]:
718	                    return 409, {
719	                        "error": "request_id already used with different content"
720	                    }
721	                # Replay the ORIGINAL result frozen at first reception; only
722	                # legacy records without a frozen summary resolve live.
723	                descriptor: dict | None = None
724	                if existing.get("height") is not None:
725	                    descriptor = {
726	                        "tip_hash": existing["tip_hash"],
727	                        "height": existing["height"],
728	                        "length": existing["length"],
729	                        "status": existing["status"],
730	                    }
731	                if descriptor is None:
732	                    descriptor = self._tip_descriptor(existing["tip_hash"]) or {
733	                        "tip_hash": existing["tip_hash"],
734	                        "height": None,
735	                        "length": None,
736	                        "status": None,
737	                    }
738	                return 200, {
739	                    "tip_hash": descriptor["tip_hash"],
740	                    "height": descriptor.get("height"),
741	                    "length": descriptor.get("length"),
742	                    "status": descriptor.get("status"),
743	                    "expires_at": existing["expires_at"],
744	                }
745	
746	            if any(tip_hash == block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain):
747	                return 409, {"error": "fork is identical to the canonical chain"}
748	            if tip_hash in self.store.forks:
749	                return 409, {
750	                    "error": "candidate fork already exists",
751	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
752	                }
753	
754	            self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
755	            self.store.syncs[key] = {
756	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
757	                "expires_at": expires_at,
758	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
759	                # The tip summary is frozen at reception: later adoption or
760	                # expiry never rewrites it, so the history always reports what
761	                # was originally delivered.
762	                "height": summary["height"],
763	                "length": summary["length"],
764	                "status": summary["status"],
765	            }
766	            self.store.append_audit_event(
767	                EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED,
768	                {
769	                    "source": source,
770	                    "request_id": request_id,
771	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
772	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
773	                    "height": summary["height"],
774	                    "length": summary["length"],
775	                    "status": summary["status"],
776	                },
777	            )
778	            try:
779	                self.store.save()
780	            except BaseException:
781	                # Roll back the candidate, its metadata and the audit event
782	                # together so a failed write never leaves one without the others.
783	                self.store.syncs.pop(key, None)
784	                self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash, None)
785	                self.store.audit_events.pop()
786	                raise
787	
788	            result = dict(summary)
789	            result["expires_at"] = expires_at
790	            return 201, result

792	    def list_fork_syncs(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
793	        """GET /v1/forks/sync — audit listing of received sync candidates.
794	
795	        Filters: ``source`` (exact), ``min_height`` and ``max_height``.
796	        ``limit`` defaults to 50 and must be 1-200; ``cursor`` defaults to 0.
797	        Every numeric value must be a plain decimal without leading zeros; a
798	        malformed value returns 400. Rows are ordered by
799	        ``(height, tip_hash, source)``; ``cursor == total`` returns an empty
800	        page, ``cursor > total`` returns 400. Each item carries
801	        ``source, request_id, tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at``.
802	        """
803	        source = params.get("source")
804	        if source is not None and (not isinstance(source, str) or not source):
805	            return 400, {"error": "source must be a non-empty string"}
806	
807	        min_height = None
808	        if params.get("min_height") is not None:
809	            min_height = _parse_decimal(params["min_height"])
810	            if min_height is None:
811	                return 400, {"error": "min_height must be a non-negative decimal"}
812	        max_height = None
813	        if params.get("max_height") is not None:
814	            max_height = _parse_decimal(params["max_height"])
815	            if max_height is None:
816	                return 400, {"error": "max_height must be a non-negative decimal"}
817	        if min_height is not None and max_height is not None and min_height > max_height:
818	            return 400, {"error": "min_height must not exceed max_height"}
819	
820	        limit = self.SYNC_DEFAULT_LIMIT
821	        if params.get("limit") is not None:
822	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["limit"])
823	            if parsed is None or not 1 <= parsed <= self.SYNC_MAX_LIMIT:
824	                return 400, {"error": "limit must be a decimal between 1 and 200"}
825	            limit = parsed
826	        cursor = 0
827	        if params.get("cursor") is not None:
828	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["cursor"])
829	            if parsed is None:
830	                return 400, {"error": "cursor must be a non-negative decimal"}
831	            cursor = parsed
832	
833	        with self.store.lock:
834	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
835	            rows: list[dict] = []
836	            for (rec_source, request_id), rec in self.store.syncs.items():
837	                if source is not None and rec_source != source:
838	                    continue
839	                descriptor = self._tip_descriptor(rec["tip_hash"])
840	                if descriptor is None:
841	                    continue
842	                if min_height is not None and descriptor["height"] < min_height:
843	                    continue
844	                if max_height is not None and descriptor["height"] > max_height:
845	                    continue
846	                rows.append(
847	                    {
848	                        "source": rec_source,
849	                        "request_id": request_id,
850	                        "tip_hash": descriptor["tip_hash"],
851	                        "height": descriptor["height"],
852	                        "length": descriptor["length"],
853	                        "status": descriptor["status"],
854	                        "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
855	                    }
856	                )
857	
858	        rows.sort(key=lambda row: (row["height"], row["tip_hash"], row["source"]))
859	        total = len(rows)
860	        if cursor > total:
861	            return 400, {"error": "cursor is beyond the result set"}

23	            self.send_response(status)

30	            try:
31	                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))

34	            if length <= 0:

202	    return LedgerHandler

205	def serve(service: LedgerService, host: str, port: int) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
206	    """Create and run the HTTP server (blocks until interrupted)."""
207	    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), build_handler(service))

1	"""Data models for transactions and blocks."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import json
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	
7	from . import crypto
8	
9	# Block lifecycle states for the confirm/rollback state machine.
10	STATUS_PENDING = "pending"
11	STATUS_CONFIRMED = "confirmed"
12	BLOCK_STATUSES = (STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_CONFIRMED)
13	
14	
15	@dataclass
16	class Transaction:
17	    sender: str
18	    recipient: str
19	    amount: int
20	    signature: str
21	
22	    @property
23	    def message(self) -> bytes:
24	        return crypto.canonical_message(self.sender, self.recipient, self.amount)
25	
26	    @property
27	    def tx_id(self) -> str:
28	        return crypto.compute_tx_id(self.message)
29	
30	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
31	        """JSON-safe representation used both for storage and API output."""
32	        return {
33	            "from": self.sender,
34	            "to": self.recipient,
35	            "amount": self.amount,
36	            "signature": self.signature,
37	            "tx_id": self.tx_id,
38	        }
39	
40	    @classmethod
41	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "Transaction":
42	        return cls(
43	            sender=data["from"],
44	            recipient=data["to"],
45	            amount=int(data["amount"]),
46	            signature=data["signature"],
47	        )
48	
49	
50	def block_header_bytes(height: int, prev_hash: str, merkle: str) -> bytes:
51	    """Deterministic serialization of the fields covered by the block hash.
52	
53	    No timestamp is included: a block with the same parent and the same ordered
54	    transactions must always hash identically.
55	    """
56	    header = {"height": height, "merkle_root": merkle, "prev_hash": prev_hash}
57	    return json.dumps(header, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
58	
59	
60	def compute_block_hash(height: int, prev_hash: str, merkle: str) -> str:
61	    return crypto.sha256_hex(block_header_bytes(height, prev_hash, merkle))
62	
63	
64	@dataclass
65	class Block:
66	    height: int
67	    prev_hash: str
68	    merkle_root: str
69	    transactions: list[Transaction]
70	    block_hash: str
71	    status: str = STATUS_CONFIRMED
72	
73	    @classmethod
74	    def create(
75	        cls,
76	        height: int,
77	        prev_hash: str,
78	        transactions: list[Transaction],
79	        status: str = STATUS_CONFIRMED,
80	    ) -> "Block":
81	        if status not in BLOCK_STATUSES:
82	            raise ValueError(f"unknown block status: {status}")
83	        ordered = sorted(transactions, key=lambda tx: tx.tx_id)
84	        merkle = crypto.merkle_root([tx.tx_id for tx in ordered])
85	        block_hash = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle)
86	        return cls(
87	            height=height,
88	            prev_hash=prev_hash,
89	            merkle_root=merkle,
90	            transactions=ordered,
91	            block_hash=block_hash,
92	            status=status,
93	        )
94	
95	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
96	        return {
97	            "height": self.height,
98	            "prev_hash": self.prev_hash,
99	            "merkle_root": self.merkle_root,
100	            "block_hash": self.block_hash,
101	            "status": self.status,
102	            "transactions": [tx.to_dict() for tx in self.transactions],
103	        }
104	
105	    @classmethod
106	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> "Block":
107	        # State files written before the status machine existed have no
108	        # "status" key; every block in such a file was final, so they load
109	        # as confirmed.
110	        status = data.get("status", STATUS_CONFIRMED)
111	        if status not in BLOCK_STATUSES:
112	            raise ValueError(f"unknown block status: {status}")
113	        return cls(
114	            height=int(data["height"]),
115	            prev_hash=data["prev_hash"],
116	            merkle_root=data["merkle_root"],
117	            block_hash=data["block_hash"],
118	            transactions=[Transaction.from_dict(t) for t in data["transactions"]],
119	            status=status,
120	        )
121	
122	    def to_summary(self) -> dict:
123	        """Response shape for GET /v1/blocks/{height}."""
124	        return {
125	            "height": self.height,
126	            "block_hash": self.block_hash,
127	            "prev_hash": self.prev_hash,
128	            "merkle_root": self.merkle_root,
129	            "status": self.status,
130	            "transaction_ids": [tx.tx_id for tx in self.transactions],
131	        }

1	"""Command line interface: send, mine, block, account, proof, confirm,
2	rollback, status, candidates, chain, adopt, export, index, sync, syncs and
3	sync-history subcommands.
4	
5	The CLI talks to a running ledger server over HTTP and prints each response as
6	a single line of JSON with exactly the same field names as the HTTP API.
7	
8	Signing a transaction locally is supported through ``send --signing-key``;
9	the key may be 32 raw hex bytes or ``@/path/to/ed25519-key.pem``. An already
10	produced signature can be passed instead with ``--from/--signature``. The
11	``candidates`` subcommand takes the candidate fork's block array (or a
12	``{"blocks": [...]}`` object) as a single JSON argument.
13	"""
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import argparse
17	import json
18	import os
19	import sys
20	import urllib.error
21	import urllib.parse
22	import urllib.request
23	from typing import Any
24	
25	from . import crypto
26	
27	DEFAULT_BASE_URL = os.environ.get("LEDGER_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8080")
28	
29	
30	# -- HTTP helpers ------------------------------------------------------------
31	
32	
33	def _request(method: str, url: str, payload: dict | None) -> tuple[int, dict]:
34	    data = None
35	    headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
36	    if payload is not None:
37	        data = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
38	        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
39	    request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
40	    try:
41	        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
42	            return response.status, json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
43	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
44	        try:
45	            body = json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))
46	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
47	            body = {"error": exc.reason}
48	        return exc.code, body
49	    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError) as exc:
50	        return 0, {"error": f"cannot reach ledger server: {exc}"}
51	
52	
53	def _emit(status: int, body: dict) -> int:
54	    print(json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False))
55	    # 2xx responses are success; anything else (incl. connection failure) is 1.
56	    return 0 if 200 <= status < 300 else 1
57	
58	
59	# -- signing key handling ----------------------------------------------------
60	
61	
62	def _load_signing_key(spec: str):
63	    """Load an Ed25519 private key from raw hex or an ``@file`` (hex or PEM)."""
64	    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
65	
66	    if spec.startswith("@"):
67	        with open(spec[1:], "rb") as fh:
68	            material = fh.read()
69	    else:
70	        material = spec.encode("ascii")
71	    stripped = material.strip()
72	    if stripped.startswith(b"-----BEGIN"):
73	        key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(stripped, password=None)
74	    else:
75	        raw = bytes.fromhex(stripped.decode("ascii"))
76	        if len(raw) != 32:
77	            raise ValueError("signing key must be 32 raw bytes (64 hex chars)")
78	        from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
79	            Ed25519PrivateKey,
80	        )
81	
82	        key = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(raw)
83	    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey
84	
85	    if not isinstance(key, Ed25519PrivateKey):
86	        raise ValueError("signing key is not an Ed25519 private key")
87	    return key
88	
89	
90	def _public_key_hex(key) -> str:
91	    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
92	
93	    return key.public_key().public_bytes(
94	        serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw
95	    ).hex()
96

101	def cmd_send(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
102	    if args.signing_key:
103	        try:
104	            key = _load_signing_key(args.signing_key)
105	        except (ValueError, OSError, TypeError) as exc:
106	            return _emit(400, {"error": f"invalid signing key: {exc}"})
107	        sender = _public_key_hex(key)
108	        message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, args.to, args.amount)
109	        signature = key.sign(message).hex()
110	    else:
111	        if not args.sender or not args.signature:
112	            return _emit(
113	                400,
114	                {"error": "provide either --signing-key or both --from and --signature"},
115	            )
116	        sender, signature = args.sender, args.signature
117	
118	    payload = {

120	        "to": args.to,
121	        "amount": args.amount,
122	        "signature": signature,

1	"""Cryptographic helpers: Ed25519 verification, SHA-256 ids and Merkle roots."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import hashlib
5	import hmac
6	import json
7	import re
8	
9	from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidSignature
10	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PublicKey
11	
12	
13	def canonical_message(sender: str, recipient: str, amount: int) -> bytes:
14	    """Deterministic byte representation of a transaction payload.
15	
16	    The payload is serialized as compact JSON with sorted keys so the same
17	    (from, to, amount) triple always yields identical bytes on every client.
18	    """
19	    payload = {"amount": amount, "from": sender, "to": recipient}
20	    return json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
21	
22	
23	def sha256_hex(data: bytes) -> str:
24	    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
25	
26	
27	def compute_tx_id(message: bytes) -> str:
28	    """SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical transaction message."""
29	    return sha256_hex(message)
30	
31	
32	def verify_signature(public_key_hex: str, message: bytes, signature_hex: str) -> bool:
33	    """Verify an Ed25519 signature (public key and signature are hex strings).
34	
35	    Returns False for malformed hex or wrong key/signature lengths rather than
36	    raising, so callers can treat every verification failure uniformly.
37	    """
38	    try:
39	        public_bytes = bytes.fromhex(public_key_hex)
40	        signature_bytes = bytes.fromhex(signature_hex)
41	    except ValueError:
42	        return False
43	    if len(public_bytes) != 32 or len(signature_bytes) != 64:
44	        return False
45	    try:
46	        public_key = Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(public_bytes)
47	        public_key.verify(signature_bytes, message)
48	    except (InvalidSignature, ValueError):
49	        return False
50	    return True
51	
52	
53	# Merkle root of an empty transaction list; fixed so genesis blocks are identical.
54	EMPTY_MERKLE_ROOT = sha256_hex(b"")
55	
56	
57	def merkle_root(tx_ids: list[str]) -> str:
58	    """SHA-256 Merkle root of the given tx ids.
59	
60	    Levels are built by hashing ``sha256(left + right)`` hex-string pairs;
61	    a lone odd node at a level is promoted by pairing it with itself.
62	    Callers normally pass ids already sorted ascending.
63	    """
64	    if not tx_ids:
65	        return EMPTY_MERKLE_ROOT
66	    level = list(tx_ids)
67	    while len(level) > 1:
68	        if len(level) % 2 == 1:
69	            level.append(level[-1])
70	        level = [
71	            sha256_hex((level[i] + level[i + 1]).encode("ascii"))
72	            for i in range(0, len(level), 2)
73	        ]
74	    return level[0]
75	
76	
77	# A SHA-256 digest rendered as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
78	_HEX64_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}")
79	
80	# Maximum Merkle depth we accept: 64 sibling levels already cover trees with up
81	# to 2**64 leaves, so a longer sibling path is necessarily malformed.
82	MAX_MERKLE_DEPTH = 64
83	
84	
85	def _is_hex64(value: object) -> bool:
86	    return isinstance(value, str) and _HEX64_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None
87	
88	
89	def is_hex64(value: object) -> bool:
90	    """True iff ``value`` is a 64-char lowercase SHA-256 hex string."""
91	    return _is_hex64(value)
92	
93	
94	def merkle_proof(tx_ids: list[str], index: int) -> list[dict]:
95	    """Sibling path from the leaf at ``index`` up to the Merkle root.
96	
97	    Mirrors :func:`merkle_root`: levels hash ``sha256(left + right)`` hex pairs
98	    and a lone odd node is paired with itself. Each returned item has a
99	    ``direction`` ("left" or "right") recording which side the *sibling* sits
100	    on relative to the path node, and the sibling's ``hash``. Items are ordered
101	    from the leaf level toward the root. Raises ValueError for an empty list or
102	    an out-of-range index.
103	    """
104	    if not tx_ids:
105	        raise ValueError("cannot build a Merkle proof for an empty tree")
106	    if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
107	        raise ValueError("index must be an integer")
108	    if index < 0 or index >= len(tx_ids):
109	        raise ValueError("transaction index out of range")
110	
111	    level = list(tx_ids)
112	    position = index
113	    siblings: list[dict] = []
114	    while len(level) > 1:
115	        if len(level) % 2 == 1:
116	            level.append(level[-1])
117	        if position % 2 == 0:
118	            # Path node is the left child; sibling sits on its right.
119	            siblings.append({"direction": "right", "hash": level[position + 1]})
120	        else:
121	            # Path node is the right child; sibling sits on its left.
122	            siblings.append({"direction": "left", "hash": level[position - 1]})
123	        level = [
124	            sha256_hex((level[i] + level[i + 1]).encode("ascii"))
125	            for i in range(0, len(level), 2)
126	        ]
127	        position //= 2
128	    return siblings
129	
130	
131	def verify_merkle_proof(
132	    tx_id: str,
133	    siblings: list[dict],
134	    merkle_root: str,
135	    block_hash: str,
136	    expected_block_hash: str,
137	) -> bool:
138	    """Verify a Merkle proof and bind it to a specific block hash.
139	
140	    Re-hashes the leaf (``tx_id``) with the sibling path from leaf to root and
141	    compares the result with ``merkle_root``; ``block_hash`` must additionally
142	    equal ``expected_block_hash``. Every malformed input (non-64-char lowercase
143	    hex hash, illegal direction, non-list path, excessive depth) and every
144	    mismatch returns False rather than raising.
145	    """
146	    try:
147	        if not _is_hex64(tx_id):
148	            return False
149	        if not _is_hex64(merkle_root):
150	            return False
151	        if not _is_hex64(block_hash) or not _is_hex64(expected_block_hash):
152	            return False
153	        if not isinstance(siblings, list) or len(siblings) > MAX_MERKLE_DEPTH:
154	            return False
155	
156	        current = tx_id
157	        for item in siblings:
158	            if not isinstance(item, dict):
159	                return False
160	            direction = item.get("direction")
161	            sibling_hash = item.get("hash")
162	            if not _is_hex64(sibling_hash):
163	                return False
164	            if direction == "left":
165	                pair = sibling_hash + current
166	            elif direction == "right":
167	                pair = current + sibling_hash
168	            else:
169	                return False
170	            current = sha256_hex(pair.encode("ascii"))
171	
172	        if not hmac.compare_digest(current, merkle_root):
173	            return False
174	        if not hmac.compare_digest(block_hash, expected_block_hash):
175	            return False
176	        return True
177	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
178	        return False

"""Entry point: ``python -m ledger`` runs the HTTP server."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

from .server import serve
from .service import DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE, LedgerService
from .store import LedgerStore, StateRecoveryError

DEFAULT_STATE_PATH = os.environ.get("LEDGER_STATE", "ledger_state.json")
DEFAULT_HOST = os.environ.get("LEDGER_HOST", "0.0.0.0")
DEFAULT_PORT = int(os.environ.get("LEDGER_PORT", "8080"))


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m ledger", description="Verifiable ledger server")
    parser.add_argument("--host", default=DEFAULT_HOST, help="bind host (default: %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PORT, help="bind port (default: %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument("--state", default=DEFAULT_STATE_PATH, help="state JSON file (default: %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--initial-balance",
        type=int,
        default=int(os.environ.get("LEDGER_INITIAL_BALANCE", str(DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE))),
        help="endowment per identity (default: %(default)s)",
    )
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        store = LedgerStore(args.state)
    except StateRecoveryError as exc:
        # Never silently start a fresh chain on corrupt/unrecoverable state:
        # report the failing location and reason, then exit non-zero.
        print(f"ledger state recovery failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    service = LedgerService(store, initial_balance=args.initial_balance)
    print(f"ledger listening on http://{args.host}:{args.port} (state: {args.state})")
    try:
        serve(service, args.host, args.port)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("ledger shutting down")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Tests for persistent source trust and the append-only audit log.

Covers POST /v1/trust/sources (201 at version 1 active, 200 idempotent
re-post, 409 on changed content, 400 on malformed input), rotate (404
unknown/revoked, 409 version mismatch, version increment), revoke (404
unknown, 409 mismatch, revoked state, 200 idempotent repeat), atomic
persistence of every change together with its audit event, GET /v1/trust
(fixed genesis hash, active unexpired sources only, allowlist preserved),
GET /v1/audit/events (source/kind filters, limit default 50 / 1-200,
cursor pagination by ascending event_id, cursor == total empty page,
cursor > total 400, items/total/next_cursor), sync reception/adoption/
expiry audit events that stay queryable after adoption or expiry,
restart durability, strict recovery rejection of corrupt trust sections
and same-generation snapshot conflicts (StateRecoveryError), plus the
HTTP and CLI surfaces.

Run: python3 tests/trust_audit_test.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest
import urllib.request
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer
from io import StringIO

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

from ledger import crypto
from ledger.cli import main as cli_main
from ledger.models import Block
from ledger.server import build_handler
from ledger.service import LedgerService
from ledger.store import LedgerStore, StateRecoveryError

KEY_A = "a" * 64
KEY_B = "b" * 64
FUTURE = 1_900_000_000


def keypair() -> tuple[Ed25519PrivateKey, str]:
    key = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    pub = key.public_key().public_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw
    ).hex()
    return key, pub


def signed_tx(key: Ed25519PrivateKey, sender: str, to: str, amount: int) -> dict:
    msg = crypto.canonical_message(sender, to, amount)
    return {"from": sender, "to": to, "amount": amount, "signature": key.sign(msg).hex()}


def make_block(genesis: Block, key, sender, recipient, amount, *, height=1, status="confirmed"):
    from ledger.models import Transaction

    return Block.create(
        height,
        genesis.block_hash,
        [Transaction.from_dict(signed_tx(key, sender, recipient, amount))],
        status,
    )


def make_fork(genesis: Block, blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
    tip = blocks[-1]
    return {
        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
        "height": tip.height,
        "length": len(blocks),
        "status": tip.status,
        "blocks": [b.to_dict() for b in blocks],
    }


class TrustAuditServiceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.state_path = os.path.join(self.tmp, "state.json")
        self.svc = LedgerService(
            LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000), initial_balance=1000
        )
        self.store = self.svc.store
        self.genesis = self.store.chain[0]
        self.key, self.pub = keypair()
        self.key2, self.pub2 = keypair()

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def register(self, source="node-1", key_hex=KEY_A, expires_at=FUTURE):
        return self.svc.register_trust_source(
            {"source": source, "public_key": key_hex, "expires_at": expires_at}
        )

    def _ensure_sync_trust(self, source: str) -> None:
        # Sync deliveries require an active trusted source. The first call
        # records a source_registered audit event; re-posts are idempotent.
        status, body = self.register(source, KEY_A, FUTURE)
        self.assertIn(status, (200, 201), body)

    # -- registration --------------------------------------------------------

    def test_register_creates_version_1_active_with_event(self) -> None:
        status, body = self.register()
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        self.assertEqual(
            body,
            {
                "source": "node-1",
                "public_key": KEY_A,
                "expires_at": FUTURE,
                "version": 1,
                "status": "active",
            },
        )
        status, audit = self.svc.list_audit_events({})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(audit["total"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(audit["items"][0]["kind"], "source_registered")
        self.assertEqual(audit["items"][0]["event_id"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(audit["items"][0]["source"], "node-1")

    def test_register_same_content_is_idempotent_200(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(self.register()[0], 201)
        status, body = self.register()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
        self.assertEqual(body["version"], 1)
        _, audit = self.svc.list_audit_events({})
        # Idempotent re-post records no second event.
        self.assertEqual(audit["total"], 1)

    def test_register_different_content_conflicts_409(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(self.register()[0], 201)
        status, body = self.register(key_hex=KEY_B)
        self.assertEqual(status, 409, body)
        status, body = self.register(expires_at=FUTURE + 1)
        self.assertEqual(status, 409, body)

    def test_register_validation_errors_400(self) -> None:
        for bad in (
            {"source": "", "public_key": KEY_A, "expires_at": FUTURE},
            {"source": "n", "public_key": "Z" * 64, "expires_at": FUTURE},
            {"source": "n", "public_key": KEY_A, "expires_at": "soon"},
            {"source": "n", "public_key": KEY_A, "expires_at": True},
            {"source": "n", "public_key": KEY_A[:63], "expires_at": FUTURE},
            ["not", "an", "object"],
        ):
            status, body = self.svc.register_trust_source(bad)
            self.assertEqual(status, 400, bad)

    # -- rotation -----------------------------------------------------------

    def test_rotate_increments_version_and_events(self) -> None:
        self.register()
        status, body = self.svc.rotate_trust_source(
            "node-1",
            {"public_key": KEY_B, "expires_at": FUTURE + 10, "expected_version": 1},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
        self.assertEqual(body["version"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(body["status"], "active")
        self.assertEqual(body["public_key"], KEY_B)
        _, audit = self.svc.list_audit_events({})
        self.assertEqual([e["kind"] for e in audit["items"]][:2],
                         ["source_registered", "source_rotated"])

    def test_rotate_unknown_or_revoked_is_404(self) -> None:
        status, _ = self.svc.rotate_trust_source(
            "ghost", {"public_key": KEY_B, "expires_at": FUTURE, "expected_version": 1}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.register()
        self.assertEqual(
            self.svc.revoke_trust_source("node-1", {"expected_version": 1})[0], 200
        )
        status, _ = self.svc.rotate_trust_source(
            "node-1", {"public_key": KEY_B, "expires_at": FUTURE, "expected_version": 2}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

    def test_rotate_version_mismatch_is_409(self) -> None:
        self.register()
        status, _ = self.svc.rotate_trust_source(
            "node-1", {"public_key": KEY_B, "expires_at": FUTURE, "expected_version": 9}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 409)

    # -- revocation ---------------------------------------------------------

    def test_revoke_lifecycle_and_idempotency(self) -> None:
        self.register()
        status, body = self.svc.revoke_trust_source("node-1", {"expected_version": 1})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
        self.assertEqual(body["status"], "revoked")
        # Repeating at the same recorded version is idempotent: 200, no event.
        status, body = self.svc.revoke_trust_source("node-1", {"expected_version": 1})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        _, audit = self.svc.list_audit_events({})
        self.assertEqual(sum(e["kind"] == "source_revoked" for e in audit["items"]), 1)
        # Wrong version conflicts.
        status, _ = self.svc.revoke_trust_source("node-1", {"expected_version": 2})
        self.assertEqual(status, 409)
        # Unknown source 404.
        status, _ = self.svc.revoke_trust_source("ghost", {"expected_version": 1})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        # Malformed version 400.
        status, _ = self.svc.revoke_trust_source("node-1", {"expected_version": "x"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    # -- GET /v1/trust ------------------------------------------------------

    def test_trust_document_filters_and_preserves_allowlist(self) -> None:
        self.register("live", KEY_A, FUTURE)
        self.register("expired", KEY_B, int(time.time()) - 1)
        self.register("revoked", KEY_A, FUTURE)
        self.svc.revoke_trust_source("revoked", {"expected_version": 1})
        self.store.allowlist["keyless-node"] = FUTURE
        self.store.save()
        status, doc = self.svc.get_trust_document()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(doc["genesis_hash"], self.genesis.block_hash)
        self.assertEqual(set(doc["sources"]), {"live"})
        self.assertEqual(
            doc["sources"]["live"], {"public_key": KEY_A, "expires_at": FUTURE}
        )
        self.assertEqual(doc["allowlist"], {"keyless-node": FUTURE})

    # -- audit pagination ----------------------------------------------------

    def test_audit_pagination_filters_and_cursor_rules(self) -> None:
        for i in range(5):
            self.register(f"n{i}", format(i + 1, "064x"), FUTURE)
        status, page = self.svc.list_audit_events({"limit": "2", "cursor": "0"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 5)
        self.assertEqual([e["event_id"] for e in page["items"]], [1, 2])
        self.assertEqual(page["next_cursor"], 2)
        status, page = self.svc.list_audit_events({"limit": "2", "cursor": "2"})
        self.assertEqual([e["event_id"] for e in page["items"]], [3, 4])
        status, page = self.svc.list_audit_events({"limit": "2", "cursor": "4"})
        self.assertEqual([e["event_id"] for e in page["items"]], [5])
        self.assertIsNone(page["next_cursor"])
        # cursor == total -> empty page
        status, page = self.svc.list_audit_events({"cursor": "5"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(page["items"], [])
        # cursor > total -> 400
        status, _ = self.svc.list_audit_events({"cursor": "6"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        # bad limit / leading zeros
        self.assertEqual(self.svc.list_audit_events({"limit": "0"})[0], 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.svc.list_audit_events({"limit": "201"})[0], 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.svc.list_audit_events({"limit": "01"})[0], 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.svc.list_audit_events({"cursor": "x"})[0], 400)
        # filters
        status, page = self.svc.list_audit_events({"source": "n2"})
        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 1)
        status, page = self.svc.list_audit_events({"kind": "source_registered"})
        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 5)
        self.assertEqual(self.svc.list_audit_events({"kind": "nope"})[1]["total"], 0)

    # -- sync events: received / adopted / expired --------------------------

    def _sync_fork(self, *, source="node-2", request_id="req-1", expires_at=None):
        block = make_block(self.genesis, self.key, self.pub, self.pub2, 10)
        candidate = make_fork(self.genesis, [self.genesis, block])
        if expires_at is None:
            expires_at = int(time.time()) + 3600
        self._ensure_sync_trust(source)
        return self.svc.submit_fork_sync(
            {
                "source": source,
                "request_id": request_id,
                "expires_at": expires_at,
                "candidate": candidate,
            }
        )

    def test_sync_received_event_persisted(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._sync_fork()
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        _, audit = self.svc.list_audit_events({"kind": "sync_received"})
        self.assertEqual(audit["total"], 1)
        event = audit["items"][0]
        self.assertEqual(event["source"], "node-2")
        self.assertEqual(event["request_id"], "req-1")
        self.assertEqual(event["tip_hash"], body["tip_hash"])
        self.assertEqual(event["expires_at"], body["expires_at"])

    def test_sync_adopted_event_survives_adoption(self) -> None:
        _, body = self._sync_fork()
        status, _ = self.svc.adopt_fork(body["tip_hash"])
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        _, audit = self.svc.list_audit_events({"source": "node-2"})
        kinds = [e["kind"] for e in audit["items"]]
        # The source's own registration event also carries source="node-2";
        # the sync events follow in append order and remain queryable.
        self.assertEqual(
            kinds, ["source_registered", "sync_received", "sync_adopted"]
        )
        # Still queryable after adoption, by kind and source.
        _, adopted = self.svc.list_audit_events({"kind": "sync_adopted"})
        self.assertEqual(adopted["total"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(adopted["items"][0]["tip_hash"], body["tip_hash"])

    def test_sync_expired_event_survives_expiry(self) -> None:
        _, body = self._sync_fork(expires_at=int(time.time()) - 10)
        # A fresh expired submission is 410 and records nothing; instead
        # register live, then force expiry and trigger the sweep.
        status, body = self._sync_fork(request_id="req-2", expires_at=int(time.time()) + 3600)
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)
        rec = self.store.syncs[("node-2", "req-2")]
        rec["expires_at"] = int(time.time()) - 5
        # Any locked operation runs the expiry sweep; query the audit log.
        status, audit = self.svc.list_audit_events({})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        kinds = [e["kind"] for e in audit["items"]]
        self.assertIn("sync_expired", kinds)
        expired = [e for e in audit["items"] if e["kind"] == "sync_expired"]
        self.assertEqual(len(expired), 1)
        self.assertEqual(expired[0]["tip_hash"], body["tip_hash"])
        # The delivered candidate fork is gone with its record...
        self.assertNotIn(body["tip_hash"], self.store.forks)
        self.assertNotIn(("node-2", "req-2"), self.store.syncs)
        # ...but the event remains queryable.

class TrustAuditHTTPTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.state_path = os.path.join(self.tmp, "state.json")
        self.svc = LedgerService(
            LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000), initial_balance=1000
        )
        self.httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), build_handler(self.svc))
        import threading

        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.httpd.server_port}"

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.httpd.shutdown()
        self.httpd.server_close()
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)

    def _request(self, method, path, body=None):
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            self.base + path, data=data, method=method,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as resp:
                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read())

    def test_http_surface(self) -> None:
        import urllib.error

        status, body = self._request(
            "POST", "/v1/trust/sources",
            {"source": "n1", "public_key": KEY_A, "expires_at": FUTURE},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        self.assertEqual(self._request("GET", "/v1/trust")[0], 200)
        status, body = self._request(
            "POST", "/v1/trust/sources/n1/rotate",
            {"public_key": KEY_B, "expires_at": FUTURE, "expected_version": 1},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        status, body = self._request(
            "POST", "/v1/trust/sources/n1/revoke", {"expected_version": 2}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        status, body = self._request("GET", "/v1/audit/events?limit=1")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["total"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(body["next_cursor"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self._request("GET", "/v1/audit/events?cursor=9")[0], 400)
        # URL-encoded source path segment.
        status, _ = self._request(
            "POST", "/v1/trust/sources/n%31/revoke", {"expected_version": 1}
        )
        self.assertIn(status, (200, 404, 409))

    def test_cli_commands_single_line_json(self) -> None:

            "trust", "add", "--source", "n1", "--public-key", KEY_A,
            "--expires-at", str(FUTURE),
        )
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(line.splitlines()), 1)

        rc, line = self._cli("trust", "export")
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        self.assertIn("genesis_hash", json.loads(line))

        rc, line = self._cli(
            "trust", "rotate", "--source", "n1", "--public-key", KEY_B,
            "--expires-at", str(FUTURE), "--expected-version", "1",
        )
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        rc, line = self._cli(
            "trust", "revoke", "--source", "n1", "--expected-version", "2"
        )
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        rc, line = self._cli("audit", "--limit", "2")
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        body = json.loads(line)
        self.assertEqual(body["total"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(len(body["items"]), 2)
        rc, line = self._cli("audit", "--kind", "source_registered")
        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(line)["total"], 1)

        # Non-2xx prints JSON and exits 1.

            "trust", "rotate", "--source", "ghost", "--public-key", KEY_B,
            "--expires-at", str(FUTURE), "--expected-version", "1",

    def test_restart_drops_invalid_candidate_keeps_canonical(self):
        b1 = Block.create(1, self.genesis.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.B, 10)])
        valid_tip = self.submit([self.genesis, b1])[1]["tip_hash"]
        with open(self.state_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            doc = json.load(fh)
        # Replace the candidate set with one bogus entry; recovery drops it
        # but must still recover the canonical chain.
        doc["forks"] = [[{"height": 0, "bogus": True}]]
        with open(self.state_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(doc, fh)
        reopened = LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000)
        self.assertEqual(reopened.forks, {})
        self.assertEqual(reopened.tip_hash(), self.genesis.block_hash)
        # The genuinely valid candidate alone round-trips fine.
        with open(self.state_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            doc = json.load(fh)
        doc["forks"] = [[self.genesis.to_dict(), b1.to_dict()]]
        with open(self.state_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(doc, fh)
        reopened2 = LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000)
        self.assertIn(valid_tip, reopened2.forks)

    def test_restart_canonical_invalid_raises_state_recovery_error(self):
        # Extend the *canonical* chain with a confirmed block, then tamper it.
        b1 = Block.create(1, self.genesis.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.B, 10)])
        self.store.chain.append(b1)
        self.store.rebuild_derived()
        self.store.save()
        with open(self.state_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            doc = json.load(fh)
        self.assertEqual(len(doc["chain"]), 2)
        doc["chain"][1]["block_hash"] = "f" * 64
        with open(self.state_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(doc, fh)
        with self.assertRaises(StateRecoveryError):
            LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000)

    def test_same_generation_conflicting_snapshots_raise(self):
        b1 = Block.create(1, self.genesis.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.B, 10)])
        self.submit([self.genesis, b1])
        with open(self.state_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            first = json.load(fh)

        # A second, self-consistent chain with different content.
        other_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        other_path = os.path.join(other_dir, "o.json")
        other = LedgerService(
            LedgerStore(other_path, initial_balance=1000), initial_balance=1000
        )
        other.submit_transaction(tx_dict(self.ka, self.A, self.B, 123))
        mined = other.mine_block()[1]
        other.confirm_block(mined["height"])
        with open(other_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            second = json.load(fh)
        self.assertNotEqual(first["chain"], second["chain"])

        gen = 99
        first["state"]["generation"] = gen
        second["state"]["generation"] = gen
        conflict_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        main_path = os.path.join(conflict_dir, "state.json")
        with open(main_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(first, fh)
        with open(
            os.path.join(conflict_dir, ".ledger-twin.gen%d" % gen), "w", encoding="utf-8"
        ) as fh:
            json.dump(second, fh)
        with self.assertRaises(StateRecoveryError) as ctx:
            LedgerStore(main_path, initial_balance=1000)
        self.assertIn("conflicting snapshots", ctx.exception.reason)

def append_audit_event(self, kind: str, payload: dict, at: float | None = None) -> dict:
        """Append an audit event in memory with the next monotonic event_id.

        The event is sealed with the append-only hash chain: its
        ``prev_hash`` is the previous event's ``event_hash`` (64 zeros for
        the first event) and ``event_hash`` is computed over that previous
        hash concatenated with the event minus its two hash fields. Does not
        save; the caller persists the event and the checkpoint together with
        the state change it describes in one atomic write. Caller must hold
        the lock.
        """
        event = {
            "event_id": len(self.audit_events) + 1,
            "kind": kind,
            "at": time.time() if at is None else at,
        }
        event.update(payload)
        prev_hash = (
            self.audit_events[-1]["event_hash"] if self.audit_events
            else crypto.AUDIT_GENESIS_PREV_HASH
        )
        event["prev_hash"] = prev_hash
        event["event_hash"] = crypto.audit_event_hash(prev_hash, event)
        self.audit_events.append(event)
        return event

    def _discover_candidates(self, directory: str) -> list[str]:
        """List the main file and sibling .ledger-* snapshots (if any)."""

        if os.path.exists(self.path):

            full = os.path.join(directory, name)

@staticmethod
    def _reseal_audit_chain(audit_events: list[dict]) -> None:
        """Re-seal a legacy audit log with prev_hash/event_hash links.

        Used once, on the single winning snapshot, to upgrade a log written
        before hash chaining existed: every event gets a ``prev_hash`` (64

        Events already sealed are left untouched. Mutates the list in place.

def test_restart_backfill_not_deduped_across_lifecycles(self) -> None:
        # A reused (source, request_id) key opens a second lifecycle with
        # content identical to the first (same candidate and even the same
        # expires_at). When the second lifecycle is also reconciled away on
        # restart, its sync_expired must be appended even though every
        # payload field matches the first lifecycle's durable event.
        source = "cycled"
        # The registry entry is short-lived; the sync record itself is not.
        self.assertEqual(
            self.register(source, KEY_A, int(time.time()) + 1)[0], 201
        )
        doc = self.candidate(self.block(amount=7))
        record_expiry = int(time.time()) + 3600
        status, body = self.sync(doc, source=source, expires_at=record_expiry)
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        tip = body["tip_hash"]
        time.sleep(1.1)  # registry entry expires while the process is "down"

        # Restart #1: the registry lapse reconciles the first lifecycle away
        # and backfills exactly one sync_expired for it.
        reopened = self._reopen()
        self.assertNotIn((source, "req-1"), reopened.syncs)
        self.assertNotIn(tip, reopened.forks)
        expiries = [e for e in reopened.audit_events if e["kind"] == "sync_expired"]
        self.assertEqual(len(expiries), 1)

        # Rotate the source back to active, then resubmit the identical key,
        # candidate and expires_at: a brand-new lifecycle (201 with a fresh
        # sync_received), never a replay of the expired one.
        svc2 = LedgerService(reopened, initial_balance=1000)
        self.assertEqual(
            svc2.rotate_trust_source(
                source,
                {
                    "public_key": KEY_B,
                    "expires_at": int(time.time()) + 1,
                    "expected_version": 1,
                },
            )[0],
            200,
        )
        status, body2 = svc2.submit_fork_sync(
            {
                "source": source,
                "request_id": "req-1",
                "expires_at": record_expiry,
                "candidate": doc,
            }
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body2)
        self.assertEqual(body2["tip_hash"], tip)
        self.assertEqual(body2["expires_at"], record_expiry)
        time.sleep(1.1)  # registry entry expires again while "down"

        # Restart #2: the second lifecycle is reconciled away too. Its
        # sync_expired MUST be appended even though source, request_id,
        # tip_hash and expires_at are all identical to the first event.
        reopened2 = self._reopen()
        self.assertNotIn((source, "req-1"), reopened2.syncs)
        self.assertNotIn(tip, reopened2.forks)
        expiries2 = [
            e for e in reopened2.audit_events if e["kind"] == "sync_expired"
        ]
        self.assertEqual(len(expiries2), 2)

# -- audit log ------------------------------------------------------------

    AUDIT_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50
    AUDIT_MAX_LIMIT = 200

    def _parse_audit_query(
        self, params: dict
    ) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, int, int] | None:
        """Parse the audit query parameters shared by events/export.

        Returns (source, kind, limit, cursor) or None after the caller has
        already answered 400.
        """
        source = params.get("source")
        if source is not None and (not isinstance(source, str) or not source):
            return None
        kind = params.get("kind")
        if kind is not None and (not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind):
            return None
        limit = self.AUDIT_DEFAULT_LIMIT
        if params.get("limit") is not None:
            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["limit"])
            if parsed is None or not 1 <= parsed <= self.AUDIT_MAX_LIMIT:
                return None
            limit = parsed
        cursor = 0
        if params.get("cursor") is not None:
            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["cursor"])
            if parsed is None:
                return None
            cursor = parsed
        return source, kind, limit, cursor

    def _audit_page(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
        """Shared filter/paginate step returning (status, page-or-error)."""
        parsed = self._parse_audit_query(params)
        if parsed is None:
            return 400, {"error": "invalid audit query parameters"}
        source, kind, limit, cursor = parsed
        with self.store.lock:
            # Sweep expired syncs first so their expiry events are visible on
            # the same page that observes the removal.
            self._prune_expired_syncs()
            items = [
                dict(event)
                for event in self.store.audit_events
                if (source is None or event.get("source") == source)
                and (kind is None or event.get("kind") == kind)
            ]
        total = len(items)
        if cursor > total:
            return 400, {"error": "cursor is beyond the result set"}
        return 200, {
            "items": items,
            "total": total,
            "limit": limit,
            "cursor": cursor,
        }

    def list_audit_events(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
        """GET /v1/audit/events — paginated append-only audit log.

        Filters ``source`` and ``kind`` are AND-combined; ``limit`` defaults
        to 50 and must be 1-200, ``cursor`` defaults to 0. Numeric values
        must be plain decimals without leading zeros. Events are ordered by
        their ascending ``event_id``; ``cursor == total`` returns an empty
        page, ``cursor > total`` returns 400.
        """
        status, page = self._audit_page(params)
        if status != 200:
            return status, page
        items, total = page["items"], page["total"]
        limit, cursor = page["limit"], page["cursor"]
        page_items = items[cursor : cursor + limit]
        next_cursor = cursor + limit if cursor + limit < total else None
        return 200, {"items": page_items, "total": total, "next_cursor": next_cursor}

    def export_audit_events(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
        """GET /v1/audit/export — hash-anchored, paginated audit log export.

        Pagination and filtering reuse GET /v1/audit/events exactly
        (``source``/``kind``/``cursor``/``limit``, same defaults and 400
        rules). Each item carries the full event including its ``prev_hash``
        and ``event_hash`` links. ``anchor_hash`` is the hash immediately
        preceding the page head — the first item's ``prev_hash``, or the
        stream tail hash (64 zeros for an empty stream) for an empty final
        page — letting an offline verifier chain successive pages.
        ``checkpoint`` is ``{event_id, event_hash}`` of the whole (unfiltered)
        stream tail, conventionally 0 / 64 zeros when the stream is empty.
        """
        status, page = self._audit_page(params)
        if status != 200:
            return status, page
        items, total = page["items"], page["total"]
        limit, cursor = page["limit"], page["cursor"]
        page_items = items[cursor : cursor + limit]
        next_cursor = cursor + limit if cursor + limit < total else None
        if page_items:
            anchor_hash = page_items[0]["prev_hash"]
        else:
            # Empty page: only reachable at cursor == total; anchor it at the
            # current stream tail so a chained verifier still binds it.
            with self.store.lock:
                anchor_hash = (
                    self.store.audit_events[-1]["event_hash"]
                    if self.store.audit_events
                    else crypto.AUDIT_GENESIS_PREV_HASH
                )
        checkpoint = self.store_checkpoint()
        return 200, {
            "items": page_items,
            "total": total,
            "next_cursor": next_cursor,
            "anchor_hash": anchor_hash,
            "checkpoint": checkpoint,
        }

    def store_checkpoint(self) -> dict:
        """The current audit checkpoint ``{event_id, event_hash}``.

        An empty stream uses 0 and 64 zeros, matching the persisted and
        recovered checkpoint convention.
        """
        with self.store.lock:
            if self.store.audit_events:
                tail = self.store.audit_events[-1]
                return {"event_id": tail["event_id"], "event_hash": tail["event_hash"]}
        return {"event_id": 0, "event_hash": crypto.AUDIT_GENESIS_PREV_HASH}
